main_result: For disjoint original sources J,{i},K, S=a·X_J, W=X_i+ell·X_K, B=beta·X_K, and nonsingular symmetric H with H_SS=0, the output (S,W,B)^T H(S,W,B) has a continuous density with ||p||inf <=12[||a||^2||beta||^2(1+||P_{beta^perp}ell||^2)|det H|]^(-1/3). For the corresponding exact-rank-three A=L^T H L this is <=12|pdet A|^(-1/3), hence <=12/s if its three nonzero eigenvalues have modulus >=s. A physical singleton S improves the constant to 6*2^(2/3).

partner_result_applied.actual_inequality: ||p||inf <=6(NM)^(2/3)|det H|^(-1/3), with N<=sqrt(2)/||a|| and M<=2/[||beta|| sqrt(1+eta^2)], giving the new constant 12 and exact pseudodeterminant cancellation.

unresolved_implication: The bare s_3(A)>=1 hypothesis does not force a fresh-coordinate wedge with an independent scalar bank. Fully source-entangled scalar/pair dependence and arbitrary additional spectrum remain open.
next_step: Seek a product-preserving routing theorem that either exposes this fresh wedge or sends its failure to a paid ridge/grouped-cross/common-plane/hub/pair-log receiver without inverting a vanishing physical minor.
